_about: MD-81/-82/-83/-88 (one outline: Boeing's MD-80 document draws and dimensions them together), built from the MD-90's measured airframe and checked against the MD-80's own sheet. Boeing's MD-80 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (Rev. 12/89) is a 1-bit scan over a printed grid (about 33 px a meter; grid lines as thick as the outlines and crossing them), so its fuselage, wing and tail are the MD-90's (md90/: a vector sheet of the same airframe) with the MD-90's 1.45 m stretch taken out ahead of the wing (plug.py on md90's snapped side and plan, --plug 13:-1.45; the front view as it is). Laid over the MD-80's own 2.2 views at their scale, those lines fall on its drawing (within a line's width on the plan's wing and tailplane, the side's fuselage and fin). The MD-80's own parts, measured on its sheet: the JT8D-200 nacelle in the side view (side.engine.anchors.json, snapped on the scan and moved into the MD-90 raster's pixels: plug.py --ppm 133.67 --nose 274 --scale 1.31765 --origin 274,1033.5 --shift 650,222), its inlet and stub pylon in the front view and the pylon in the plan (plan.engine.json, front.engine.json, already in the MD-90 rasters' pixels). The composed files: side.snap.json is md90's plugged side with side.engine's engine.top and engine.bottom; plan.snap.json is md90's plugged plan without engine.outer/inner (the nacelle's middle is the front view's) and with plan.engine's pylon; front.snap.json is md90's front with front.engine's inlet and pylon. The doors' and windows' places along the body are the MD-80 sheet's own (its side view at 133.67 px a meter: nose 274, the printed 41.58 m to the tail cone 5832), their heights the MD-90 sheet's (the scan draws every door 0.1-0.2 m higher on the tube than the vector sheet and 2.7.2's section, which puts the door sill 0.53 m below the centerline). Cockpit panes: the MD-90's (the same nose).

windows.note: Each window's place along the body measured on the MD-80 sheet's side view (2.2), which draws them (closed outlines; 45 ahead of the aft service door, 6 more behind it, the last ones beside the nacelle's inlet); their height and width the MD-90 sheet's (the same cabin windows).

meta.name: McDonnell Douglas MD-80 (MD-81, MD-82, MD-83, MD-88)

sources.title: Boeing, MD-80 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (Rev. 12/89), 2.2 General Airplane Dimensions: Model MD-81, -82, -83 and -88; 2.7.2 Passenger Entrance and Service Door Clearances
sources.note: One outline for the MD-81, -82, -83 and -88: the document draws and dimensions them together. Its 2.2 is a 1-bit scan over a printed grid (about 33 px a meter, the grid's lines as thick as the outlines and crossing them), so the fuselage, wing, fin and tailplane are the MD-90's measured lines with its 1.45 m plug ahead of the wing taken out (tools/trace/md82/), checked against this sheet: laid over its views at their scale they fall on its lines within a line's width along the fuselage, wing and tailplane, and the printed figures (45.02 m overall, 32.85 m span, 12.25 m tailplane, 3.35 m width) within 0.4%. Where the two sheets differ the shape keeps the MD-90's vector drawing of the same tail: the MD-80 scan draws the tail cone's underside up to 0.35 m higher and the fin's leading edge about 0.3 m further forward. This sheet's own: the JT8D-200 nacelle (side view; its inlet and stub pylon in the front view, 2.70 m from the centerline as printed, where the plan draws it at 2.62 m), the pylon in the plan, and the doors' and cabin windows' places along the body (the side view, at the printed 41.58 m from the nose to the tail cone). The main entry door sits within 2 cm of 2.7.2's printed 4.38 m to its middle; the right side's service door is placed from 2.7.2's partial plan (27 in wide, 48.5 in tall, 4.51 m to its middle, its sill with the main door's). The scan draws every door 0.1-0.2 m higher on the tube than the MD-90's vector sheet and 2.7.2's section (its door sill 0.53 m below the centerline), so the doors' and windows' heights are the MD-90 sheet's. The side view draws the tube 1.4% short of the printed 3.61 m and the MD-90's 3.6% tall: the fuselage is fit to the printed height (fit_height.py). Confidence medium: the scan, and the tail's two drawings.

sources.title: Boeing, MD-90-30/-30ER Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (MDC K9099, October 2002), 2.2 General Airplane Dimensions, 2.3 Ground Clearances
sources.note: The fuselage, wing, fin and tailplane, as measured for the MD-90 (shapes/MD90.json), with its 1.45 m stretch ahead of the wing taken out: the MD-90 is the MD-80's airframe with that plug (the two documents' fuselage lengths, 43.03 m and 41.58 m, and wheelbases, 23.52 m and 22.05 m, differ by it).
